nodes.label: An applicant cannot currently have driving privileges suspended, revoked or denied in South Dakota or another state when obtaining a South Dakota driver license.

nodes.label: The licensing eligibility list requires an applicant to have no unpaid fines for moving traffic violations.

nodes.label: The handbook’s licensing eligibility requirements include being legally present in the United States.

nodes.label: An application and residence-address documents are required each time a person applies for a South Dakota license or identification card.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Photocopied documents do not meet the handbook’s licensing-document requirements.

nodes.label: For renewal of a license or identification card that has a star on its front, the current starred credential is a required document.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: The starred-credential renewal route requires two documents proving a South Dakota physical address, each less than one year old.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Under the starred-credential renewal list, noncitizens and people transferring from another state must provide evidence of lawful United States status.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A person whose name differs from the starred credential being renewed must provide a marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order proving the change.

nodes.label: For replacement of a South Dakota credential that had a front-side star, the primary document may be a certified United States birth certificate, valid United States passport or passport card, citizenship or naturalization certificate, valid permanent-resident card, valid employment-authorization card, or a foreign passport with United States visa and I-ninety-four.

nodes.label: Replacing a South Dakota credential that had a front-side star requires two physical-address documents from South Dakota that are less than one year old.

nodes.label: A name change on the starred-credential replacement route requires proof through a marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A new South Dakota license or identification-card applicant, including an interstate transfer applicant, needs one document establishing date of birth, identity and lawful status or presence.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: For the initial-application identity document, the handbook recommends choosing a document bearing the current full legal name when possible so a name change need not be documented.

nodes.label: An unexpired United States passport or passport card is an accepted primary identity document for a new South Dakota license or identification card.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A state-issued United States birth certificate used as primary identity proof must be certified and carry the issuing authority’s stamp or raised seal; a hospital birth certificate is unacceptable.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A Puerto Rico birth certificate used for primary identity proof must have been certified as issued on or after July one, two thousand ten.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Accepted State Department proof of a birth abroad includes Form FS-two hundred forty, DS-one thousand three hundred fifty or FS-five hundred forty-five.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: An unexpired permanent-resident card on Form I-five hundred fifty-one is accepted as primary identity proof for a new South Dakota credential.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: An unexpired employment-authorization card on Form I-seven hundred sixty-six is accepted as primary identity proof for a new South Dakota credential.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: An I-ninety-four arrival-and-departure record with a photograph attached and a Temporary Proof of Lawful Permanent Resident stamp is an accepted primary identity document.

nodes.label: Name-change proof is required when the applicant’s current full legal name differs from the primary identity document or a previously issued South Dakota credential used a different name from that document.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Name-change documents must link the selected identity document to the current full legal name, using more than one document when needed to complete that link.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Accepted name-change documents include a certified marriage certificate or a court name-change order issued through a petition, divorce, annulment or adoption.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A marriage certificate used for name-change proof must be a certified copy from the vital-statistics office or equivalent agency where the marriage occurred, bearing the issuing authority’s stamp or raised seal.

nodes.label: A certificate issued by a church, chapel or similar institution is not acceptable marriage-certificate proof for the licensing name change.

nodes.label: A court order used for name-change proof must show the previous full legal name, court-ordered full legal name and date of birth, and bear the official court seal.

nodes.label: A date stamp or filing stamp does not qualify as the official court seal required on a name-change order.

nodes.label: Photocopies and faxed copies of a name-change court order are unacceptable.

nodes.label: Social Security proof must show the current name and complete Social Security number on a Social Security card, W-two, Social Security Administration one thousand ninety-nine, other one thousand ninety-nine, or paystub.

nodes.label: A person eligible to work who lacks a Social Security number must obtain and present one.

nodes.label: A minor may use a parent’s address documents only when the accompanying parent’s name appears on those documents.

nodes.label: Physical-address evidence may include utility or phone bills, bank statements, pay or earnings statements, mortgage documents, rent receipts, tax documents, homeowners or renters insurance, and accredited-school transcripts or report cards.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: An examiner may review other items bearing the applicant’s address as possible physical-address evidence.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A full-time traveler using a South Dakota mail-forwarding address must complete a Residency Affidavit.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: The full-time-traveler address route requires a receipt from a South Dakota hotel, motel, campground or RV park establishing a stay of at least one night within the previous year.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: The full-time-traveler address route also requires the South Dakota personal-mailbox contract or agreement.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: For the full-time-traveler route, one document no more than one year old must prove the personal-mailbox service address, using a mailbox-business receipt or mail bearing that address.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: Maintaining a residence in another state disqualifies a person from the handbook’s full-time-traveler category.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: An honorably discharged veteran may request Veteran on a South Dakota license or identification card by adding discharge proof to the ordinary required documents.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: The veteran-designation proof list allows a DD-two hundred fourteen showing honorable active-duty discharge, a county or tribal veterans-service-officer certificate of honorable status, DD Form two Retired, DD Form 2A Reserve Retired, or NGB Form twenty-two.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal fact coverage for this topic; no official exam weight is asserted.

nodes.label: A male license applicant aged eighteen through twenty-five must state that he registered with Selective Service or authorize DPS to send the information needed to register him.
